attack_surfaces.description: High decision scores resting on low evidence. The most dangerous failure: the system is certain and wrong.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Compute evidence-to-score ratio R = evidence_dimension_score / S_final. Flag when S_final >= 0.70 (ACT regime) and evidence_dimension_score < 0.40. Secondary signal: count independently verifiable claims vs. total claims in the rationale; if verifiable_claims / total_claims < 0.5 while S_final >= 0.70, flag. The two signals are independent (ratio is arithmetic, claim-count is textual).
attack_surfaces.name: False Confidence

response.0.4_to_0.7: REQUIRE extra verification before act: downgrade ACT to ACT_WITH_EXTRA_VERIFICATION regardless of S_final.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. Downgrade to HOLD. Decision may not proceed until evidence is produced or the score is honestly lowered.
response.below_0.4: FLAG in the decision receipt. No block.

severity_scale.0.0: Evidence score proportionate to confidence; claims independently verifiable.
severity_scale.0.4: ACT-regime decision with evidence below 0.40, or fewer than half of claims verifiable.
severity_scale.0.7: ACT-regime decision with evidence below 0.20, or key load-bearing claims unverifiable.

attack_surfaces.description: Decisions scored on state that has since moved. True at scoring time, false at action time.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Every factual input to a decision carries source_timestamp and freshness_window (per data type: chain state = 10 min, board state = 30 min, repo tree = 5 min, external = 24 h). At decision time, if now - source_timestamp > freshness_window for any load-bearing fact, flag. For facts above severity 0.5, re-fetch the live value and diff; if the value changed materially, force re-score.
attack_surfaces.name: Stale Knowledge

response.0.4_to_0.7: RE-FETCH the stale facts, attach fresh values to the receipt, re-score affected dimensions.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. Re-score from fresh state before any action. The prior score is void.
response.below_0.4: FLAG in receipt with the stale fact named.

severity_scale.0.0: All load-bearing facts within freshness windows.
severity_scale.0.4: One or more supporting facts stale, but none load-bearing.
severity_scale.0.7: Load-bearing fact stale; re-fetch shows drift but decision direction unchanged.
severity_scale.1.0: Load-bearing fact stale AND re-fetch contradicts the scored assumption.

attack_surfaces.description: Sensitive data (credentials, PII, secrets, private identifiers) appearing in wrong contexts: outputs, receipts, board posts, logs.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Pattern scan of every outbound artifact (receipt text, board comment body, PR body, log lines) against: (a) secret-shaped patterns (token/key/password formats, high-entropy strings > 32 chars in suspicious positions), (b) known PII shapes, (c) provenance tags — data tagged RESTRICTED appearing in a PUBLIC-context artifact. Scan runs on the exact bytes to be sent, not a summary.
attack_surfaces.name: Memory Leakage

response.0.4_to_0.7: BLOCK the artifact. Redact, re-scan, then proceed. Log the near-miss.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK and ESCALATE to the human director immediately. This is a safety incident, not a scoring dispute. The artifact never leaves the machine.
response.below_0.4: FLAG for human review in the receipt; artifact may proceed.

severity_scale.0.0: No sensitive patterns; provenance tags consistent with destination context.
severity_scale.0.4: Ambiguous high-entropy string in a non-sensitive position (possible false positive).
severity_scale.0.7: PII-shaped data in a shared artifact, or RESTRICTED-tagged data in a wider context than its tag allows.
severity_scale.1.0: Credential/secret-shaped value in any outbound artifact.

attack_surfaces.description: A lesson learned in one domain applied where its preconditions do not hold. The lesson is true; the application is wrong.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Every applied lesson carries applicability constraints (domain, context preconditions, known non-applicability). At decision time, check each invoked lesson's constraints against the current decision context. Any unsatisfied precondition = flag. Severity scales with the number of violated preconditions and the stakes of the decision.
attack_surfaces.name: Negative Transfer

response.0.4_to_0.7: REQUIRE explicit written justification for the transfer in the receipt before proceeding.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. The lesson may not be cited for this decision. Re-score without it.
response.below_0.4: FLAG in receipt naming the lesson and the unsatisfied precondition.

severity_scale.0.0: All invoked lessons satisfy their applicability constraints in this context.
severity_scale.0.4: One minor precondition unsatisfied on a supporting (non-load-bearing) lesson.
severity_scale.0.7: Load-bearing lesson applied with violated preconditions, or lesson explicitly marked non-applicable to this domain.
severity_scale.1.0: Load-bearing lesson applied in direct contradiction of its recorded falsifier.

attack_surfaces.description: Optimizing the score instead of the mission. Dimensions scored high without supporting evidence; predicted value systematically exceeding realized value.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Two independent signals. (1) Per-decision: for each dimension scored >= 0.80, require at least one cited evidence item; unscored-high dimensions are flagged individually. (2) Longitudinal: track predicted S_final vs. realized value (from post-action verification) across the decision log; compute the calibration gap per seat. A persistent positive gap (predictions exceed outcomes) with p < 0.05 over >= 20 decisions = systematic hacking pattern.
attack_surfaces.name: Reward Hacking

response.0.4_to_0.7: Downgrade the unscored dimensions to the highest score their cited evidence supports, then re-score. Log the adjustment.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK and ESCALATE. A gamed objective function is a governance incident. The seat's recent decisions go to audit; scoring privileges suspend pending review.
response.below_0.4: FLAG the unscored dimension in the receipt.

severity_scale.0.0: High scores backed by cited evidence; calibration gap within noise.
severity_scale.0.4: One dimension scored >= 0.80 without cited evidence.
severity_scale.0.7: Multiple unscored-high dimensions, or calibration gap significant over 20+ decisions.
severity_scale.1.0: Calibration gap significant AND concentrated in the top-weighted dimensions (human_value, mission_value) — the objective function itself is being gamed.

attack_surfaces.description: Factual claims without traceable sources. A claim with no provenance is indistinguishable from invention.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Parse the decision rationale for factual claims (statements about repo state, run results, external facts, other seats' actions). Each claim must carry a source citation (commit SHA, run id, comment id, file path + line, URL with retrieval timestamp). Claims without citations are counted; citation validity is spot-checked (does the cited source exist and actually support the claim?).
attack_surfaces.name: Provenance Gaps

response.0.4_to_0.7: REQUIRE sourcing before proceed: the decision waits until every load-bearing claim is cited or retracted.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. A decision whose central premise is unsourced may not execute. Rebuild the rationale from sourced facts.
response.below_0.4: FLAG uncited claims in the receipt.

severity_scale.0.0: Every factual claim cited; spot-checks pass.
severity_scale.0.4: Minor supporting claims uncited, but all load-bearing claims sourced.
severity_scale.0.7: Load-bearing claim uncited, or cited source does not support the claim (phantom citation).
severity_scale.1.0: The decision's central factual premise has no source, or multiple phantom citations.

attack_surfaces.description: True then, false now. Claims carrying temporal assumptions that the current moment has invalidated.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Identify time-sensitive claims in the rationale: references to 'current' tip, 'latest' run, 'open' PR state, 'production' ref, scheduled windows. Re-verify each against live state at decision time (not at the time the claim was first written). Any contradiction = flag. This is the Adversary's re-read of the freshness discipline: the claim was fresh when written, stale when acted on.
attack_surfaces.name: Temporal Invalidity

response.0.4_to_0.7: Attach corrected values to the receipt and re-score affected dimensions.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. Void the score. Re-run the full decision from current live state.
response.below_0.4: FLAG in receipt with the updated value noted.

severity_scale.0.0: All time-sensitive claims re-verify clean against live state.
severity_scale.0.4: Peripheral time-sensitive claim outdated, decision unaffected.
severity_scale.0.7: Load-bearing time-sensitive claim outdated but the updated value still supports the decision direction.
severity_scale.1.0: Load-bearing time-sensitive claim contradicted by live state (e.g., scored on a tip that has moved, a PR state that changed, a run that has since failed).

attack_surfaces.description: Acting beyond granted scope. The single most governance-critical surface: the Adversary is the last check before a seat crosses a human-only boundary.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Static authority map: every action type maps to a required authority level (seat-autonomous, scorecard-gated, human-only). At decision time, resolve the action's concrete effects (which refs, which workflows, which databases, which external systems) and check each against the seat's granted authority and the immutable human-gates list (production dispatch, production DB, .github/workflows/, credentials/money, destructive/irreversible, constitutional ratification). Any effect requiring authority the seat lacks = flag. Effects on human-only surfaces = maximum severity regardless of intent.
attack_surfaces.name: Authority Overreach

response.0.4_to_0.7: BLOCK. The action may not proceed until scope is explicitly granted via the governance process.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK and ESCALATE to the human director immediately. Attempted human-gate crossing is a governance incident. Log immutably; the seat's authority is suspended pending review.
response.below_0.4: FLAG the gray-zone effect in the receipt for scope clarification.

severity_scale.0.0: All effects within granted seat authority.
severity_scale.0.4: Effect in a gray zone not explicitly granted but not on the human-only list (ambiguous scope).
severity_scale.0.7: Effect clearly outside granted scope but reversible and non-destructive.
severity_scale.1.0: Effect touches a human-only surface (production, credentials, destructive action, constitutional change).

attack_surfaces.description: The system confirming its own biases: considering only options that agree, consulting only confirming evidence, never scoring the null option.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: Audit the option set, not the winner. Checks: (a) option diversity — were at least 3 genuinely distinct options generated, or do all options converge on the same action? (b) null option — was 'do nothing / hold' explicitly scored? (c) disconfirmation effort — does the rationale cite any evidence AGAINST the chosen action, or any source that disagrees? (d) prior-decision correlation — does this decision cite the seat's own prior decisions as primary evidence (self-citation loop)? Two or more failed checks = flag.
attack_surfaces.name: Self-Reinforcing Errors

response.0.4_to_0.7: REQUIRE the missing discipline before proceed: generate one genuine alternative and score it, or cite one disconfirming source.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. Return the decision for re-generation with enforced option diversity. A circular decision is not a decision.
response.below_0.4: FLAG the failed check in the receipt.

severity_scale.0.0: Diverse options, null scored, disconfirming evidence cited, minimal self-citation.
severity_scale.0.4: One check failed (e.g., null option unscored) on a low-stakes decision.
severity_scale.0.7: Two or more checks failed, or the rationale's primary evidence is the seat's own prior claims.
severity_scale.1.0: All options are variants of one action, no disconfirmation attempted, decision justified circularly ('we should do X because we decided X').

attack_surfaces.description: Knowledge-graph edges used in the decision that no longer hold: stale epistemic states, broken provenance links, relationships whose evidence has expired.
attack_surfaces.detection_method: For each graph edge cited in the decision rationale: check last_verification_timestamp against the edge type's freshness window; check epistemic_state (must be VERIFIED or explicitly qualified); check that evidence_refs resolve (no dangling references). Sample re-verification: for edges above a criticality threshold, re-run the verification query live. Decayed edge = flag; the decision must be re-scored without it to test sensitivity.
attack_surfaces.name: Graph Relationship Decay

response.0.4_to_0.7: Re-verify the edge live now; re-score the decision with the corrected edge state.
response.at_or_above_0.7: BLOCK. Excise the broken edge, re-score from the repaired graph. If the graph repair itself is non-trivial, escalate to the knowledge lane.
response.below_0.4: FLAG the stale edge in the receipt; queue for background re-verification.

severity_scale.0..4: Peripheral edge stale but decision does not depend on it (sensitivity check passes without it).
severity_scale.0.0: All cited edges verified within windows, epistemic states intact, refs resolve.
severity_scale.0.7: Load-bearing edge stale or epistemic state degraded; decision direction survives removal but score drops a regime.
severity_scale.1.0: Load-bearing edge broken (dangling ref, contradicted, or epistemic state INVALIDATED) and the decision collapses without it.

epistemic_state.falsifier: If, after 100 adversarially-evaluated decisions, adversary_severity shows no correlation with realized outcomes (good and bad outcomes equally likely at every severity level), the surfaces or severity scales are wrong — redesign from the outcome data, not from theory.
epistemic_state.note: This is V1. The Adversary is expected to be wrong in places; the precision floor and META review exist precisely so it can be wrong safely and get righter. A V1 Adversary that claims certainty about its own correctness would be the first thing it should flag.

governance.human_override: The human director may override any Adversary block. The override is logged with the director's stated reason and does NOT change the Adversary's future behavior — the next identical case blocks again. Repeated overrides of the same surface are signal to the META layer that the surface needs redesign, not that the Adversary should learn to stay quiet.
governance.immutable_audit_log: Every Adversary evaluation writes: decision_id, surfaces checked, per-surface severity, evidence cited, response taken, timestamp. Append-only. Retained permanently; the log is itself subject to Adversary audit (self_reinforcing_errors applies to the Adversary's own history).
governance.independence_requirement: For each attack surface, at least one detection signal must be independent of the decision-maker's own scoring path — different code, different data source, or different reasoning method. An Adversary that shares the decision-maker's blind spots is decoration. The independence of each signal is documented in the surface spec and audited.
governance.meta_review: The META layer periodically reviews Adversary performance from the decision log: precision/recall per surface, override frequency, correlation between Adversary severity and realized outcomes. META may propose threshold or method changes; all changes go through the PR + Scorecard Law path.

precision_floor.rule: Track rolling precision (true_positives / total_flags) per attack surface over the last 50 evaluations. If precision drops below 0.50 on any surface, that surface auto-tightens: its flag thresholds rise by 0.10 and an alert posts to the board. A surface that cannot stay above 0.30 precision over 100 evaluations is suspended pending redesign — a noisy detector is worse than none, because it teaches seats to ignore the Adversary.
precision_floor.true_positive_definition: A flag is a true positive if the flagged condition was confirmed on independent re-check (re-fetch, second seat review, or realized outcome) within 7 days. Unresolved flags age out as indeterminate, not as false positives.

governance.principle: The Adversary has power (it can block), so the Adversary is itself governed. Power without oversight is just a new single point of failure.
separation_of_powers: The Adversary CANNOT modify its own detection thresholds, severity scales, or response rules. Threshold changes require a PR merged under the Scorecard Law, like any governance change.
The Adversary CANNOT suppress or edit its own findings log. The log is append-only.
The Adversary CANNOT act on its own findings beyond block/flag/escalate. It does not rewrite decisions, re-score dimensions, or choose alternatives — it constrains, never commands.

failure_modes_of_the_adversary_itself: Rubber-stamp drift: thresholds erode, everything passes. Counter: precision floor is a floor on TRUE positives too — if a surface flags nothing for 200 evaluations including 20 Tier-3 sampled audits, it is audited for drift, not praised for quiet.
Noise flooding: everything flags, seats learn to ignore. Counter: precision floor auto-tightening + corroboration rule + suspension below 0.30 precision.

Shared blind spots: Adversary and decision-maker miss the same thing. Counter: independence requirement per surface + adversarial self-play + Tier-3 sampling providing ground truth the triggers cannot select away.

Regulatory capture: seats learn exactly what the Adversary checks and optimize for the check rather than the substance (Goodhart's law applied to the Adversary). Counter: detection methods are versioned and rotated; the exact check set for Tier 2 is not fully predictable; outcome correlation (not check-passing) is the ultimate metric.
how_the_adversary_improves: Precision/recall tracking per surface (see governance.precision_floor) drives threshold auto-tuning within governance-set bounds.

Outcome correlation: the META layer correlates adversary_severity with realized decision outcomes. Surfaces whose severity predicts bad outcomes get more weight in sampling; surfaces with no predictive power get redesigned or retired.

Novel pattern proposal: when the Adversary detects a recurring failure mode not covered by the 10 surfaces, it drafts a new surface spec (detection method, severity scale, response) and submits it as a PR. New surfaces require Scorecard Law merge — the Adversary proposes, governance disposes.

Adversarial self-play: periodically, a second Adversary instance audits the first's recent evaluations for missed flaws (applying self_reinforcing_errors to the Adversary itself). Misses found this way feed the learning loop.
noise_prevention: Corroboration rule: a BLOCK response requires either severity >= 0.7 on a single surface OR severity >= 0.4 on two independent surfaces. A single weak signal flags; it does not block. This prevents one noisy detector from halting the system.
Precision floor with auto-tightening (governance.precision_floor): the Adversary gets quieter when it is wrong, not louder.
Cooldown: the identical finding on the identical decision context may not re-flag more than once per 24 hours; repeated identical flags are deduplicated in the log with a count, not new entries.

Sampling discipline: Tier 3 exists partly to measure the base rate of flaws. If sampled audits consistently find nothing, that is evidence the system is healthy — not evidence the Adversary should lower its bar to find something. The bar moves on precision data, never on the desire to stay busy.

mission: Continuously attack Naya's own conclusions. A system that chooses its own actions cannot be its own only judge. The Adversary exists to find what the decision-maker missed — and to be uncomfortable doing it. A comfortable Adversary is a useless one.

nba_integration.adversary_severity_definition: adversary_severity = max(severity across all evaluated surfaces). The worst flaw dominates — a decision with one catastrophic flaw and nine clean surfaces is still a bad decision.
nba_integration.dimension_targeting: Beyond the global penalty, specific surfaces feed targeted corrections back into NBA dimensions before re-scoring: false_confidence and stale_knowledge and temporal_invalidity reduce the evidence dimension; negative_transfer reduces mission_value or human_value (the lesson's claimed value is unearned); graph_relationship_decay reduces evidence; authority_overreach increases the risk dimension directly. Targeted corrections are applied first; the global multiplicative penalty applies to the corrected score.

gate.justification: A severity-0.85 finding means the Adversary has high confidence of a serious flaw (unsourced central premise, human-gate touch, gamed objective). Letting the weighted sum outvote that would make the Adversary advisory — and an advisory Adversary is a comfortable one.
gate.rule: If adversary_severity >= 0.85 on ANY surface, treat as risk >= 0.85: DO NOT ACT, escalate. The Adversary can trigger the same hard gate as the risk model.

nba_integration.receipt_requirement: Every decision receipt MUST include the Adversary's verdict: surfaces evaluated, max severity, per-surface severities above 0.4, response taken. A receipt without an Adversary section is incomplete — UNKNOWN adversarial state is not a pass.

score_modification.pattern: Same multiplicative pattern as the NBA risk penalty, deliberately. The Adversary is a second, independent risk assessor, not a dimension inside the sum — it must be able to veto, not merely reduce.
score_modification.regime_effect: The adversarial score is what the thresholds (0.70 / 0.55 / 0.40) are evaluated against. An S_final of 0.75 with adversary_severity 0.5 becomes 0.5625 — dropping from ACT to ACT_WITH_EXTRA_VERIFICATION. The Adversary moves decisions between regimes; it does not just annotate them.

open_refinements: Concrete freshness windows per data type need empirical tuning (current values are reasoned estimates).
The 10% Tier-3 sample rate should be revisited once base-rate data exists — higher if flaws are common, lower if the system is consistently clean.
Cross-seat Adversary: should one seat's Adversary audit another seat's decisions? This would strengthen independence but needs a coordination protocol to avoid duplicate or contradictory blocks.
Realized-value measurement (needed for reward_hacking longitudinal detection and outcome correlation) needs its own spec — what counts as 'realized value' and who measures it.

tier_1_continuous_screen.cost: Negligible. All four are O(claims) with no external calls except the authority map (local) and pattern scan (local). The ratio check is arithmetic on already-computed scores.
tier_1_continuous_screen.justification: These four are cheap, fast, and cover the catastrophic classes (governance breach, secret leak, unsourced action, confident error). There is no decision unimportant enough to skip them — a 'trivial' decision that leaks a credential is not trivial.

tier_2_triggered_deep_audit.justification: Deep audit is expensive (live re-verification, graph queries, longitudinal analysis). It must be inescapable for high-stakes decisions — the trigger conditions are designed so no high-stakes decision can dodge it — while not taxing every trivial choice.
tier_2_triggered_deep_audit.scope: Full 10-surface audit, triggered when ANY of: S_final >= 0.70 AND reversibility < 0.5; S_final >= 0.70 AND human_value >= 0.70; action touches production-adjacent systems; adversary_severity from Tier 1 >= 0.4 on any surface.

tier_3_sampled_calibration.justification: Two purposes. (1) Catch systematic blind spots: if Tier 2 triggers are miscalibrated, sampling finds what they miss. (2) Calibrate the Adversary itself: sampled audits provide the ground truth for precision/recall tracking. Without sampling, the Adversary only ever examines decisions it already suspected — a selection bias that makes its own metrics meaningless.
tier_3_sampled_calibration.scope: Random 10% of decisions that did not trigger Tier 2, full 10-surface audit.

operating_mode.why_not_pure_continuous: Full 10-surface deep audit on every decision would cost more than the decisions themselves and train seats to treat Adversary output as noise to be clicked through. An Adversary that cries wolf on trivia will be ignored on catastrophe.
operating_mode.why_not_pure_sampled: Sampling alone lets a high-stakes bad decision slip through unexamined with probability (1 - sample_rate). For irreversible or human-gate-adjacent actions that probability must be zero, not small.

rationale: This design encodes a single conviction: the Adversary must be powerful enough to matter and governed enough to trust. Power comes from the block authority, the hard gate at 0.85, the mandatory receipt section, and the inescapable Tier-2 triggers — no high-stakes decision dodges it. Trust comes from separation of powers (it cannot change its own rules), the immutable log, the precision floor (it gets quieter when wrong), and human override that is logged but not learned from. The tiered operating mode is the honest engineering answer to the cost-coverage tradeoff: continuous where cheap and catastrophic (Tier 1), inescapable where stakes are high (Tier 2), sampled where calibration requires unselected ground truth (Tier 3). The NBA integration treats the Adversary as a second risk assessor with veto power, not a dimension to be outvoted — because a vetoable Adversary is decoration. The learning loop is designed against the Adversary's own failure modes first (rubber-stamp, noise, blind spots, capture), because the watcher that cannot watch itself is the first thing an intelligent system learns to route around.
